evidence.says: Carleton identifies Jennifer V. Evans as a history professor with a PhD from SUNY Binghamton. Her supervision list matches the entry: Eedy, Freeland and Whitehouse in 2016, Hogg in 2017, and Lundrigan in 2019, with corresponding dissertation subjects or titles.
Her own CV lists a PhD in Modern European History from SUNY-Binghamton in 2001 and employment in Carleton History beginning in 2001.
Jean H. Quataert’s institutional CV, p. 19, lists Jennifer Evans among PhD dissertations directed, with Reconstruction Sites, the subtitle using Postwar Berlin, 1944-58, and the year 2001.

The museum identifies its fellow Jennifer Evans as a Carleton history professor who completed her PhD at SUNY Binghamton, and names her Reconstruction Sites dissertation, using Postwar Berlin, 1944-1958 in the subtitle.

Josie McLellan, Love in the Time of Communism, p. 4, note 13, cites Jennifer Evans’s Reconstruction Sites dissertation at Binghamton University, State University of New York, in 2001, using Divided Berlin, 1944-1958 in the subtitle. The note also connects Evans to Life Among the Ruins, listed on her Carleton profile.

notes: Institution, year and dissertation match linked AHA record 20758. The title above follows the publisher citation, which matches the AHA wording with the date range expanded. Quataert and the museum use Postwar Berlin in place of Divided Berlin; this title variation does not indicate a different author or doctorate. No thesis catalogue record was located.
